decisionsTitle: Internal notes on a registration, for organizers and administrators
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-15, from his phone:** «ca și Admins, trebuie să putem lăsa comentarii pe fiecare înscriere în parte, doar pentru organizatori și administratori». His standing word on the open points was «YOLO»: they are decided below, each with its reason, and the owner may turn any of them.

**Decision.** A registration carries **internal notes** — what the organizers tell each other while they organise the event («cere tricou S», «vine cu o oră mai târziu»). Plain text in the author's own language (no bilingual rule: nothing a visitor reads), at most 2000 characters, line breaks kept. They live in one new table, `registration_notes` (migration `0162`, expand only: id, `registration_id` `ON DELETE CASCADE`, `author_staff_user_id` `ON DELETE SET NULL`, `body`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `deleted_at`).

**Who (BR-REQ-060-01).** The Organizer, the Administrator and the Superadministrator read and write them, through one new predicate, `canKeepRegistrationNotes` — the same set as `canReadRegistrations`, but its own name so that «may read the list» and «may keep notes» can part without a page asking one when it means the other. The Tehnic role, the volunteer, the Redactor and a member get nothing: the card is not drawn, and every function of `registrations/notes.ts` and both presses refuse FORBIDDEN, whatever the page drew (the Tehnic role and the volunteer never reach the registration's page at all, §289). **Delete** is narrower: its author, or an Administrator (`canManageRegistrations`). There is no edit: a wrong note is deleted and written again, so the trail never has to say «changed».

**Amends §289 («the Organizer reads the whole list and changes nothing on a registration»).** An explicit exception, and the reason it is one: the Organizer still changes nothing *on the registration* — no state, no place, no number, no answer, no email — and a note is not the registration, it is what the organizers say to each other about it. «Reading against changing» (§289) now has this one writing line, drawn at the note and nowhere else. The rule of §10.2/§15.11 that cancel, erase, rename, resend and the printing mark stay Administrator-only is unchanged.

**Amends §67 (the desk shows a name, a state and a number, never more).** The race-day desk shows no note, to any role, and neither do the CSV, the spreadsheet, the public list or any email: none of those queries reads the table, and `tests/unit/registrations/notes-never-leave.test.ts` lists the only files that import it (the registration's page, its two presses, the list, the person's record and the card), so a new reader is a reviewed edit of that list.

**Where it shows.** On the registration's page, a named, folded card «Note interne» (`Panel`, glyph `internalNotes`) whose closed line counts the notes — «3 note» / «nicio notă», `countForm`'s three keys, no ICU plural — with the notes newest first (the author's display name as the trail shows it, and when), «Adaugă o notă» (one textarea, «Salvează nota», the form comes back with the words in the box after a refusal, with JavaScript off too) and «Șterge» (asks first, on the notes the reader may delete). It opens by itself after a save or a delete and for `#note-interne`. On the registrations list, a small marker — the sticky-note glyph and the count in the row's words, a 44-pixel link to the card — on rows that have notes, from one grouped count over the page's ids; the Administrator sees it too.

**Privacy (§754's paragraphs, §418, BR-REQ-053-01).** A note is personal data about the participant. (a) The privacy notice's TEMPLATE gains one sentence in section 2's paragraph on the registration's history, in Romanian and English: the organizers may keep internal notes about a registration for organising the event (art. 6(1)(f) GDPR), only the organizers and administrators see them, they are deleted with the registration, and an access request is answered with them. **Template only**: the texts in force never move; the club approves a version made from it, and §639's digest tells the Administrators the template is newer. (b) «Toate datele unei persoane» lists the person's live notes — the words, when, the event and **the author's role, not their name** — and counts them in the export's audit row without a word; the trail below it keeps the rows `registration.note_added` and `registration.note_deleted` (when) but prints no name for them, on the page and in the file. (c) Erasing the registration erases its notes: the foreign key cascades, so the erase, the retention sweep and an event's hard delete all do, and the trail's erase row names nothing of the words. (d) The trail's `registration.note_added` and `registration.note_deleted` name who and when and carry an empty metadata, never the words.

**Decided without the owner («YOLO»).** (1) **A delete empties the words.** The brief asked for a soft delete that keeps the audit; the audit never needed the words, so `deleted_at` is stamped and `body` emptied in one write: the row stays only as the anchor of the trail, and nothing about a person survives a click on «Șterge». (2) **The author's role, not name, in the person's record.** What an access request owes the person is what is held about them and the kind of recipient who read it (art. 15(1)(c)); a colleague's name is the colleague's own personal data (art. 15(4)). (3) **No filter «Cu note»** on the list: the list's filters are shared with the export (`/api/admin/registrations/export` reads the same parameters), and a filter that answers «which registrations have notes» is one more way for the count to leave the screen that may see it; the marker and the search by name serve the same job. (4) **Notes on any registration**, a cancelled or test row too, and **no cap on how many**: a limit would be a rule nobody asked for. (5) **The warning against health data is words, not a check**: the help line says «Nu scrie date medicale sau alte date sensibile» and nothing scans the text.

**For the lawyer, not decided here.** (a) The limits of art. 15 on a note: whether one may be withheld where it would reveal another person's data (art. 15(4)), and whether a note's author may be named on request. (b) The temei — art. 6(1)(f), legitimate interest in organising the event — and the sentence's «nu și tu» (the person does not see the notes, only receives them on an access request). (c) The retention: a note lives as long as its registration (§324's sweep), with no shorter period of its own. (d) Whether the privacy notice's section 7 should name it.

**Refused.** Rich text, attachments and @mentions; a note visible to the participant; a bilingual rule; an edit; a note on the desk, in the CSV or on the public list; a mail or notification when a note is added; a role that may read the list but not keep notes; storing the words in the trail.
changelogLine: - **Internal notes on a registration** — «Note interne»: organizers and administrators leave plain-text notes on each registration, with a count marker on the list; never on the desk, in an export or on the public list, deleted with the registration, and listed in «Toate datele unei persoane»; the privacy notice's template says so. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given a registration's internal notes («Note interne»), when the Tehnic role, the volunteer, the Redactor or a member reads, counts, adds or deletes one, then the service and both presses refuse FORBIDDEN, whatever the page drew; the Organizer, the Administrator and the Superadministrator keep notes through `canKeepRegistrationNotes`, an Organizer deletes only their own note and an Administrator any, and the Organizer still changes nothing on the registration itself (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an Organizer or an Administrator on a registration's page, when they save a note in «Note interne», then the card shows it newest first with its author's display name and the moment, its closed line counts «3 note» / «nicio notă», the trail records `registration.note_added` with who and when and an empty metadata, the registrations list marks the row with the count, and a refused note (empty, or past 2000 characters) comes back with the words still in the box; «Șterge» asks first, empties the words and records `registration.note_deleted` the same way; the race-day desk, the CSV, the spreadsheet, the public list and every email carry no note (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a registration with internal notes, when an Administrator erases it, then its notes go with it — the foreign key cascades, soft-deleted rows too — and the trail keeps who erased and why, with no word of any note (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the privacy notice's template in both languages, when it is read, then section 2's paragraph on the registration's history says once that the organizers may keep internal notes about a registration for organising the event, that only the organizers and administrators see them, that they are deleted with the registration and that an access request is answered with them; the texts in force do not change until the club approves a version made from it (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given an Administrator opening «Toate datele unei persoane» or downloading its file, when the person's registrations have live notes, then each is listed with its words, its moment, its event and the author's role — never the author's name, and the trail beside them names nobody for adding or deleting a note — a deleted note holds no words and is not listed, and the export's audit row counts the notes without a word (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
